name: a small patch of alligator cracking — a net of three or four small polygons outlined by dark grey-black cracks, one plate slightly lifted, drawn as a transparent decal on old asphalt
label: wasteland_ruins/road-crack-c

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: asphalt patch with crack net and lifted plate, seen from above

answer.evidence: The whole 48x48 sprite is a flat, uniformly grey asphalt field with a brown border that is the same on all four sides. The column scans show a texture of mid-grey #524b49 with lighter and darker speckles and a small dark crack net around rows 19-29. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical face. The brown rows at the bottom (45-47) match the top rows (0-1) and the left and right edges, so they read as a frame rather than a south face. This is a flat decal seen from directly above, which matches the 'flat' kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's measured facts match or beat the references. It has 8 visible tones per tile against 7 for paving and 3 for grass, and 0% near-flat coverage, so no 5x5 flat fills. Only 13% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the crack lines lean warm/brown-grey instead of being a black sticker line, which counts as dark_material_tone. By eye, the asphalt is mottled with speckle and tonal variation, and the cracks form a small polygon net with a lifted plate. The shading is shallower than the paving reference, at about 4 clear steps against 5-6, and the crack net is small and low-contrast. That is acceptable for a sparse decal on old asphalt, so I rate it slightly below the reference but passable.

surfaces.part: asphalt patch with crack net (flat decal)

answer.evidence: The drawing is a 48x48 flat decal seen straight from above: grey asphalt with lighter mottling, a dark crack net around rows 19-29 (x~22-34), and a brown dirt border on the edges. The only horizontal dark/brown band is at rows 44-47, and this is a ground edge, not a vertical face. There is no front face, no eave shadow and no side face. Reads as a flat plate, as expected for a flat floor decal.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 8 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass, 0% near-flat coverage, and only 13% neutral dark edge pixels, so the dark pixels carry a tint. By eye the piece is weaker than the numbers suggest. The asphalt is a murky dark grey-brown field with only about 3-4 lightness steps and light speckle, while the paving reference has distinct per-stone highlights, mid tones and dark joints. The crack net is tiny, low-contrast and reads as one faint ringed mark in the centre, not three or four clear polygons with one lifted plate. The lifted plate has no visible highlight or shadow step. The brown frame around the patch looks like a sticker border, not a transparent decal edge. It is not flat, but it is thinner and less crafted than the Beodeul references, so I fail it on the benefit of the doubt.
